subject: Request: penetration test findings & remediation timeline after anomalous auth activity
messages:
From: security@medisync.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: cto@medisync.com
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 15:21:00 -0700
Subject: Unusual auth events — request for penetration test report and remediation timeline

Hi Karthik,

We observed a cluster of failed logins followed by a handful of successful logins from a source IP range we don't usually see in our telemetry (see attached logs). Our SOC is treating this as an elevated concern while we investigate potential account misuse. Given the timing and that MediSync has active integrations that rely on Redwood tokens, procurement/legal have asked for the most recent external penetration test report and a summary of open/high remediations.

Could you please provide: 1) the latest penetration test report or a redacted summary we can share with our security team, 2) a list of outstanding high/critical findings and expected remediation ETA, and 3) any relevant incident context (e.g., whether this activity correlates with known platform maintenance or deployments).

We appreciate a response within 24 hours if possible — procurement has paused some escalated actions pending this.

Thanks,
Aisha Rahman
Head of Security, MediSync Health
security@medisync.com

[Attachment: medisync_auth_events_excerpt.log (text)]

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: security@medisync.com
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unusual auth events — request for penetration test report and remediation timeline

Thanks Aisha — I appreciate the heads up and I’m sorry for the disruption. Looping in Dylan from Security and Grace from Customer Success to coordinate. I’ll also make sure our legal/compliance team is aware of the procurement hold.

Dylan — can you confirm the scope of our most recent external pen test and whether we can share (redacted) artifacts with MediSync? If there are any open high/critical items tied to the auth stack (token issuance, session management, SSO), please include the current remediation ETA.

Grace / Marissa — please keep MediSync updated on the commercial/procurement side while we triage.

I’ll stand by to get a redacted summary over to them today.

— Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: security@medisync.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 17:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unusual auth events — request for penetration test report and remediation timeline

Karthik / Aisha,

Thanks for flagging. Quick summary from engineering/security: our last third-party external penetration test was completed in 2025-11 (Q4 2025). Scope included the authentication stack (JWT issuance, refresh token flows), exposed API endpoints in the hosted API, and our admin console. The vendor performed authenticated and unauthenticated tests against our hosted endpoints and internal admin paths.

What we can share now:
- pen_test_summary_redwood_2025Q4_redacted.pdf (attached) — executive summary, findings by severity, remediation status. Sensitive exploit POC details are redacted per our vendor contract.
- remediation_tracker_RED-4321.csv (attached) — current list of open findings with owners and planned ETA.

Status relevant to your auth concerns:
- No confirmed compromise of token signing keys or KMS-held secrets.
- There was a medium severity finding in 2025Q4 around session timeout handling for legacy admin sessions; mitigation completed 2026-01-12 and verified by our internal tests.
- Two low/medium web findings remain open; neither affects token issuance/validation flow. Both have target remediation by 2026-03-20.

Regarding the anomalous login cluster you reported: initial checks show the successful logins originated from client-side token usage (valid tokens) rather than token issuance requests. That suggests credential- or token-exfiltration at the client side or reuse of leaked tokens rather than a server-side issuance compromise. We’ve opened an internal investigation and will share any updates.

I’ve included the redacted summary as requested. If MediSync needs the full vendor report for their procurement/legal review, we have a standard ND A + data handling addendum we require before releasing full test artifacts — I can route that to your legal team.

— Dylan Brooks
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: pen_test_summary_redwood_2025Q4_redacted.pdf]
[Attachment: remediation_tracker_RED-4321.csv]

From: security@medisync.com
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, cto@medisync.com
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unusual auth events — request for penetration test report and remediation timeline

Dylan,

Thanks for the quick summary and the redacted materials — that helps. A couple of follow-ups from our SOC and legal: 1) procurement insists on reviewing the full vendor report under NDA before they will clear continued access for certain integrations; 2) they also want affirmation that the medium finding you mentioned (legacy admin session timeout) cannot be used to escalate to tenant-level token theft.

Can you: a) share the standard NDA / handling addendum and an expected timeline for full vendor report access, and b) provide a brief technical note addressing attack paths from the legacy session timeout to token exfiltration (or a statement that they are not exploitable in combination with known Redwood architecture).

If possible, can we schedule a 30-minute bridge tomorrow with your security/eng lead to go over the technical detail (MediSync timezone PST). Procurement would like confirmation before end of day tomorrow.

— Aisha
Aisha Rahman | Head of Security, MediSync Health

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Aisha — thanks for the clarity. Next steps from Redwood: 1) Dylan will send our standard NDA + handling addendum within the hour (we’ll include a proposed 48-hour review window for the vendor report access); 2) Dylan will also prepare a short technical note on the legacy session timeout finding and explicit confirmation of whether that could lead to tenant-level token theft — initial answer: event looks client-side and mitigations are in place, but we’ll provide the written confirmation on the bridge; 3) I’ll set up a 30-minute call for tomorrow at 14:00 PST with Dylan + our infra lead (Grace) and include your SOC and procurement leads.

Grace / Marissa — can you coordinate scheduling and procurement notes? I’ll track the request in our support queue: RED-4321 and add foreseeable timeline items to the remediation tracker.

We’re treating this as a priority and appreciate the quick coordination.

— Karthik
